speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I see you are experiencing neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness. To understand the cause, can you tell me exactly where the pain radiates and which specific fingers are affected by the tingling?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of diabetes and hypertension, could you describe the nature of the weakness in your hands—specifically, is it affecting your grip strength or fine motor skills like buttoning a shirt? Additionally, do you notice any relief in your symptoms when you tilt your head to one side?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

The presence of fasciculations, absent reflexes, and progressive weakness alongside a history of paresthesias is highly suggestive of motor neuron disease. Given your age and the specific combination of upper and lower motor neuron signs, I am requesting images of your cervical and lumbar spine to rule out compressive myelopathy, though the clinical picture strongly points towards ALS.
